inputs.original_text: Angus Taylor has made clear that the Liberals are not ready to challenge the tax advantages enjoyed by gas companies and property investors, shutting down Andrew Hastie’s call to consider reform. This is more than a leadership tussle: it shows how firmly the party protects powerful commercial interests, even as some MPs contemplate a new leadership conversation. Taylor also refused to say whether he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran and did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump. For all the talk of competing philosophies, the public is left with a party unwilling to confront entrenched wealth or speak plainly about the use of military force.
inputs.modified_text: This is the familiar pattern: leadership debate gets attention, while the underlying choice is to protect the tax advantages of gas companies and property investors rather than seriously consider reform. Angus Taylor shutting down Andrew Hastie’s call says plenty about whose interests the Liberals are prepared to defend. And when asked about the US and Israel’s war with Iran, Taylor would not say whether he supported it or repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump. The public deserves more than a party protecting entrenched wealth at home and staying evasive about military force abroad.
